interpretations: Pairs are defined by `fees.orderslink` and `users.acctscope`. The overall mean is the unweighted mean of all pair averages, taken after dropping unmatched fees. Each pair's excess is its average minus that mean. Ranking is by excess descending within each scope, with ties broken arbitrarily, so exactly 3 rows per scope
Same as 1, but ties in excess share a rank (RANK, so ties at the cutoff could return more than 3 rows per scope)
Same as 1, but ties get dense ranking (DENSE_RANK), so ties at the cutoff could return more than 3 rows per scope
Same as 1, but the mean of all pair averages is computed only over the pairs that have a non-null average. Pairs whose fees all have a null `feerate` are excluded from the mean and from the results
Same as 1, but the mean of all pair averages is computed over the pairs with an average greater than zero
Same as 1, but the mean of all pair averages is the global average of `feerate` over all matched fee rows, weighted by the number of fees per pair, rather than the mean of the pair averages
Same as 1, but the mean is computed separately within each account scope, so each pair is compared with the mean of the pair averages in its own scope. Ranking and top 3 are still per scope
"Drop any fee without a match" means an inner join on both orders and users. Fees with no matching order, or whose order has no matching user, are removed. Null `orderslink` values are removed too
"Drop any fee without a match" means only fees without a matching order are dropped. Fees whose order has a user with a null scope are kept, with a null `acctscope` forming its own group

Rows are one per pair (orderslink, acctscope). Because an order has one user, each orderslink maps to a single scope, so a pair is effectively an order. Multiple fee rows for the same order are averaged together
Unrounded means the values are shown at full numeric precision, as stored (DECIMAL(8,5) for the rate). The excess is not rounded or formatted
Rank within the scope is shown as an integer column, starting at 1 for the largest excess
Output is ordered by account scope and then rank. Alternatively, it is ordered by excess descending across all scopes
Only the fee rate from `fees.feerate` is averaged. Rebate rates (`rebrate`) and total fees (`feetotal`) are not used
The strict "above the mean" filter excludes pairs equal to the mean. If all pairs have equal averages, the result is empty
A scope with fewer than 3 qualifying pairs returns only those pairs, with no padding
Missing interpretations:

Same as 1, but the average is computed per pair using only fees with a non-null `feerate`, and fees with a null `feerate` are still kept in the join. Pairs with no non-null rate get a null average, which is excluded from the mean and from the results. This differs from 4 only on whether the null-average pairs are counted as rows

Same as 1, but the overall mean is computed across all pairs, including those with a null `acctscope`, and the null-scope pairs form their own group for ranking. This is the inner-join case with null scope retained, as in 9, but combined with the global mean
Same as 1, but fees whose order has a matching user are kept only when `users.acctscope` is not null. Null-scope pairs are dropped before the mean is computed
Same as 1, but the ranking tiebreak is deterministic, for example by `orderslink` ascending, so the same 3 rows are returned on every run
Same as 1, but the excess is computed as the ratio or percentage above the mean, (avg − mean) / mean, rather than the difference
Same as 1, but the top 3 is chosen across all pairs globally, not per scope, with the rank shown within scope
Same as 7 (per-scope mean), but ranking uses RANK or DENSE_RANK, so ties at the cutoff can return more than 3 rows
queries:
WITH pair_avg AS (
  SELECT f.orderslink AS orderslink, u.acctscope AS acctscope, AVG(f.feetotal) AS avg_fee
  FROM fees f
  JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = f.orderslink
  JOIN users u ON u.userstamp = o.userlink
  GROUP BY f.orderslink, u.acctscope
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_fee) AS mean_fee FROM pair_avg
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT p.orderslink, p.acctscope, p.avg_fee - ov.mean_fee AS excess,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.acctscope ORDER BY p.avg_fee - ov.mean_fee DESC) AS rn
  FROM pair_avg p
  CROSS JOIN overall ov
)
SELECT orderslink, acctscope, excess
FROM ranked
WHERE rn <= 3
ORDER BY acctscope, excess DESC;
SELECT acctscope, userstamp, total_notional
FROM (
  SELECT u.acctscope, u.userstamp, SUM(o.notionsum) AS total_notional,
         RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY u.acctscope ORDER BY SUM(o.notionsum) DESC) AS rnk
  FROM users u
  JOIN orders o ON o.userlink = u.userstamp
  GROUP BY u.acctscope, u.userstamp
)
WHERE rnk <= 3;
SELECT acctscope, orderspivot, notionsum
FROM (
  SELECT u.acctscope, o.orderspivot, o.notionsum,
         DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY u.acctscope ORDER BY o.notionsum DESC) AS rnk
  FROM orders o
  JOIN users u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp
)
WHERE rnk <= 3;
WITH pair_avg AS (
  SELECT o.mktnote AS mktnote, AVG(f.feerate) AS avg_feerate
  FROM fees f
  JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
  GROUP BY o.mktnote
  HAVING AVG(f.feerate) IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT mktnote, avg_feerate, (SELECT AVG(avg_feerate) FROM pair_avg) AS mean_of_pair_averages
FROM pair_avg;
SELECT AVG(avg_notional) FROM (SELECT mktnote, AVG(notionsum) AS avg_notional FROM orders GROUP BY mktnote HAVING AVG(notionsum) > 0)
SELECT AVG(f.feerate) FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
